facts.quote: Ghost recommends a four-step trust flow: **show who you are, emphasize who already trusts you, demonstrate value, and stay consistent**

facts.fact: The Adwave article recommends a six-part order for an About page: plain-language headline, short positioning statement, real people, proof elements, story and values, and next step.
facts.quote: Use this order on the page:

facts.quote: A checklist infographic detailing six essential trust signals to help improve business website credibility and customer conversion.

facts.fact: The page advises placing one or two high-confidence trust signals near the top of an About page.
facts.quote: Place one or two high-confidence signals near the top so visitors get immediate reassurance.

facts.fact: National Positions recommends short paragraphs, bullet points, easy-to-find contact information, and reduced visual noise in website design to build trust.
facts.quote: National Positions recommends short paragraphs, bullet points, easy-to-find contact information, and reduced visual noise

facts.fact: The page recommends doing a manual review of About page content every quarter to remove former team members, expired certifications, outdated screenshots, and claims that can no longer be backed up.
facts.quote: Then do a manual review every quarter.

facts.fact: Orientation Agency, a third party cited by the page, highlights HTTPS, accessible contact information, and published policies as basic trust signals for website visitors.
facts.quote: **HTTPS, accessible contact information, and published policies**
